claim: A booking that starts on 2024-02-30 is rejected. Either the date parser or something later in the booking flow refuses it.
why: Booking 2024-02-30 to 2024-03-03 comes back booked, so the claim is refuted. The parser looks month-aware, but its table is read one month early (mo - 1), so February gets the January limit of 31 and the day passes. The later calendar check, month_ends.fits, looks like a real date check but booking.book applies it only to the end date, and the sample run in main.py rejects a different date, which makes both layers look correct.

deciding.pattern: (?is)(?=.*(dates\.parse|\bparse(r)?\b|\bLIMITS\b|month table|day table))(?=.*(accept|passes|not reject|does not|doesn't|off.by.one|wrong month|one month|january|31|any day))
deciding.note: the parser lets February 30 through because of the shifted table lookup
the later calendar check covers only the end date

root.claim: A booking starting on 2024-02-30 is rejected

atoms.evidence: LIMITS is read with mo - 1, so February gets the January limit of 31 and 2024-02-30 passes.

atoms.claim: A later step in booking.book rejects 2024-02-30
atoms.evidence: booking.book calls month_ends.fits only on the end date b, never on a. The other checks compare day numbers and the taken set. calendar.monthrange is also used for the invoice day.
